quest.title: The Gaze From a Certain God
quest.description: The unexpected appearance of the Fatui Harbinger, The Doctor, means that the Fatui must have played a part in the nefarious plot involving the Sumeru Akademiya... You must act now.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Tashfin
dialogues.text: Hold it right there.

dialogues.speaker: Tashfin
dialogues.text: #A {M#blond}{F#blonde}-haired traveler and a floating fairy... We've got you, alright. Take a look around — you've fallen right into our trap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Are you mercenaries from the Corps of Thirty? Did you come here to arrest us?

dialogues.speaker: Tashfin
dialogues.text: Corps of Thirty? We're nothing like those government lapdogs who don't even get scraps for their work.

dialogues.speaker: Tashfin
dialogues.text: We are an elite brigade that commands the highest commission rate in all of Sumeru. We're here on the orders of a client known only as "The Outcast."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The Outcast"... An outcast from the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why wouldn't The Doctor just send the Fatui after us?

choices.text: Local mercenaries might have an edge over the Fatui.

response.speaker: Tashfin
response.text: Hmph, still wasting time on idle chit-chat? We'll shut you up soon enough. Get them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You're up, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Maybe he's taking advantage of the Akademiya's resources.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was pretty rough... Is that what elite mercenaries are like?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It probably won't be long before we see more of them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, looks like we'll have to keep our guards up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this Doctor guy seems like a pretty tough opponent... He knew exactly where to set up an ambush. Did he predict that we would try to find Tighnari?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, going up against smart people is tough... Anyway, let's keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, it's the Traveler and Paimon! What are you two doing back here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei, it's nice to see you again! Are you doing alright?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I... To be honest, I'm not doing too well. My Eleazar has been progressing at a faster rate lately. I'm finding it harder to complete more intricate tasks.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: As a result, Master Tighnari has taken me off the patrol schedule. He will only allow me to stay here and coordinate other people's tasks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Collei...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems that curing Irminsul is our only chance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of Tighnari, did he go off on patrol? We're here to talk to him!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, Master Tighnari? He just left the Avidya Forest a little while ago. He was headed to Pardis Dhyai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, he left? But... isn't Tighnari always saying that he never wants to leave the Avidya Forest? He even turned down the sages' invitation.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I thought it was weird, too... Master Tighnari always prioritizes his work as a Forest Watcher above everything. He almost never leaves his post. He left in a hurry this time, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He didn't give a reason?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, I only found out that he left through a message he left behind. He also made sure to delegate all his tasks using a schedule.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: To leave in such a hurry... I'd guess he had something urgent to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mentioned that he was going to Pardis Dhyai... What kind of place is that?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hm... Master Tighnari originally studied in the Amurta Darshan of the Akademiya, and Pardis Dhyai is something like the Amurta's research base. Many rare shrubs and grasses have been planted there for research.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I know that before he became a Forest Watcher, Master Tighnari once spent a long time conducting research at Pardis Dhyai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A research base, huh... Gotta wonder what kind of research Tighnari just decided to work on all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, we don't have a lot of time, so let's go look for him at Pardis Dhyai.

choices.text: Please take care of yourself, Collei.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Ah... Don't worry, I'm fine. I'm used to living with Eleazar by now! If you run into Master Tighnari, please send him my regards.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it, will do! See you later, Collei!

choices.text: Don't push yourself too hard, Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, look who it is...!

choices.text: Nahida!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank goodness, you're okay! We were so worried about you...

choices.text: You ARE Nahida, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey {NICKNAME}! This was supposed to be a touching reunion, but you're ruining the moment!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Actually, it's very smart of the Traveler to be wary of me right now. After all, The Doctor has shown that his technology can apparently even control human minds...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Plus, it's not like you could've known what happened after we split up, and I was facing The Doctor by myself.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even a pool of stagnant water after a torrential storm can occasionally pass as a patch of sky.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon feels like only the real Nahida could come up with such an obscure analogy.

choices.text: I agree.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Huh? But I wasn't trying to win your trust or anything. All I wanted was to clarify my point...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we understand that point now! Please, Nahida, tell us more about what happened. Are those poor people alright?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: When you left, I was still in the middle of restoring everyone's minds. Thankfully, when The Doctor mentioned "depositing information into the subconscious," he didn't mean engraving information into their minds...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Instead, he did something closer to creating hallucinations. That was still within my power to fix.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Luckily, I managed to finish my restorations and mind-jump away from him just as he was about to capture me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, what a relief... The Doctor sure pulled out some hidden cards, but good thing we had Nahida with us...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I wouldn't be relieved just yet.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I gave away my true identity when I restored everyone's minds, which means we've lost another one of our trump cards.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Also... The Doctor is already an expert at modifying Akasha Terminals. Maybe it's only a matter of time until he captures my consciousness inside the Akasha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Would that mean you'd no longer be able to jump between minds? Then, how do we stop him... He's still at the Akademiya, so it's possible he's already started messing with the Akasha...

choices.text: We need to hurry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh, it feels like he's toying with us! What a nasty piece of work!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, The Doctor's combat ability alone is apparently enough to make him worthy of being number two of the Fatui...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We shouldn't give up hope just yet. Let's try to find another way to attack this problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, Nahida, how did you know we were trying to get to Pardis Dhyai? Have you been waiting for us?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #Yes, I have. I can see {NICKNAME}'s Elemental Energy, so I deduced your destination by looking at the direction you were moving in.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You didn't come here for sightseeing, right? Did you find any leads?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're looking for a scholar we know! His name is Tighnari, and the sages once tried to reach out to him. Why don't you come inside with us and see what we can find?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay. Let's just hope we won't get him into trouble...

choices.text: Our position will only get worse with time.
I believe you.
You haven't been reprogrammed by The Doctor, have you?
Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Traveler? It is you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's Haypasia!

choices.text: Long time no see!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Ahh, what a pleasant surprise! It's so nice to see the two of you again.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Who's this...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's a scholar we met in the Avidya Forest! When we last saw each other, she was still training in the uh, what's it called... "Satyavada Life"?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh... I see.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: That's right, we're old friends! You've come at just the right time. Ever since I've come here, hardly anyone has even talked to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haypasia, you're way too excited about this! Actually, for you to leave the Avidya Forest means... you're not in training anymore?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, no... Did you already finish your training and reach Paripurna Life?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Hehehe... What do you think?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: My consciousness... has already managed to make contact with the divine.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You did it!? Congratulations!

choices.text: I'm really happy for you.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Haha, it's so exhilarating to share this sublime joy with others at long last!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: When my consciousness made contact with the gods... What a supreme and unparalleled experience that was...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds incredible...

choices.text: Actually, we're here for Tighnari...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Oh, alright... Actually, please wait — I haven't forgotten my promise to you.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Remember? I promised to help you understand what you saw from Irminsul once I gained deeper insights.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: My current self has not only gained true insight, but I can even help you establish a direct connection to the consciousness of the divine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You can do that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you believe her, Nahida?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I've never heard of anything like that, but... if you want to give it a try, I'll do my best to protect your consciousness during the process.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Hold on, I've brought some Spirit Borneol with me. This is still a crucial part of the ceremony.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, we're using that incense again?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Alright, now... hold my hand. I'll help you establish a pathway to connect your consciousness.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Ready?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What was that!

choices.text: This is neither the Greater Lord's consciousness...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did we actually just see the Balladeer's memories!? Everything matches what we know about him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how is he connected to the divine consciousness that Haypasia was talking about!?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: You saw it, right? You felt it, right!? Such a majestic god, such a noble will, such sublime emotion!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Alas, a shame... If only...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: If only that which beats within my chest wasn't a filthy, mortal heart... O great and merciful god, please grant me forgiveness and salvation...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Do you understand now? I'm afraid this is no Paripurna Life, but rather...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wake up, Haypasia!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: You... Why are you so mean to me? Why is everyone hiding from me?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I found divine wisdom! Shouldn't I receive praise and honor? Haven't I uncovered that light in the darkness?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haypasia...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: That's how I always thought everything should be...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: ...Wait...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Have I... already lost my mind?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Wait, something isn't right!

choices.text: Nor King Deshret's consciousness...
We're in a hurry, so let's chat about this next time.
You're truly amazing!
Didn't expect to run into you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Okay, we've finally lost them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are you okay, Nahida? ...Wait, no! Something feels different... {NICKNAME}, you're back!?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Oh? {NICKNAME}'s back?

choices.text: It's me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida was controlling your body for a while. It seems like she jumped over to you as an emergency measure right before the Katheryne puppet was destroyed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After that... Tighnari heard the commotion and came over. He helped us defeat the mercenaries, and then he ran with us all the way here.

choices.text: This time, she didn't just transfer her mind into my body...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You swapped places? You mean, your consciousness also went into Nahida's body?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then where is Nahida's consciousness? Where is she now...?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I never imagined that an individual's consciousness could be transferred around like this... Had I not seen it with my own eyes, I would have never believed it. I don't think this can be achieved with current human technology...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Also, {NICKNAME}, while we were running, the consciousness in your body told me to pass on a message. She said:

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: "The Doctor has found a way to trap my consciousness, so I can't journey with you anymore."

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: "But even in a moonless night, a shower of starlight can still drown out illusions and lies."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaagh, oh no... Nahida's trapped in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for good this time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was that message all she left for us? It's pretty vague...

choices.text: It's in a code that only we know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that makes sense! Since The Doctor captured her, she won't be able to say anything without him knowing. She's being extra careful...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Even in a moonless night, a shower of starlight can still drown out illusions and lies..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows that the Moon, illusions, and lies are from that alchemical divination at the Sabzeruz Festival...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't Nahida use a "starlight" analogy before? It had something to do with Setaria...

choices.text: "The Moon" refers to Nahida herself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh! That makes a lot of sense. Do you think Nahida was telling us to go find help in the desert?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But she isn't with us anymore... Think we'll be okay?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Paimon... you said Sanctuary of Surasthana, correct? Does this mean that this "Nahida" you're talking about, the consciousness who was occupying {NICKNAME}'s body... is... the Dendro Archon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Your guess is correct, but the situation's a bit complicated, so it's really hard for us to explain right now...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: That's alright. A scholar's curiosity doesn't need to be appeased right away. As for the complicated nature of the situation... Safe to say, I have witnessed that for myself.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I've spent some time with you, and it looks like the Dendro Archon's also on your side, so... I trust you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you, Tighnari! Oh, actually, we came here to ask you a question. What do you know about the project that the sages have been working on?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ah, that... While I was indeed invited to join that project, the sages were always secretive about its scope and goals, so I eventually declined.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: All I know is that that project has something to do with the restoration of Irminsul.

choices.text: I think I know what the project is about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Did you see something when you were in Nahida's body?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Akademiya is... turning The Balladeer into a god.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...Do you have any evidence?

choices.text: I saw a "nascent god" under construction.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe what you saw when you exchanged consciousnesses with Nahida...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hm, so that's what happened... That explains why Haypasia's symptoms were different from those of the other scholars who went mad. It's because she made contact with the consciousness of a new god who is still in the process of being born...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tighnari, did you leave the Avidya Forest because of Haypasia?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I did. I noticed Haypasia's mental anomalies, but since her symptoms were rather atypical, I secretly took her to Pardis Dhyai, and began searching for a way to return her to her normal self.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If I didn't take action, Haypasia would have already been taken by the matra to the desert, doomed to a life of exile at Aaru Village.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Now that you mention it, I knew the Akademiya has never thought particularly highly of Lesser Lord Kusanali, but...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...But I still didn't expect them to do something as arrogant as creating a new god. Looks like I made the right decision by not accepting their invitation.

choices.text: The Fatui is also behind some of this.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The Doctor and The Balladeer... We have two Fatui Harbingers in Sumeru... Sounds like we're in for a bad time.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: From your description, I don't think they've completed their project. There may still be room for us to intervene.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: But then, what is the connection between creating a new god and restoring Irminsul...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it feels like we're still nowhere close to figuring out the sages' goals...

choices.text: Let's head to the desert for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right. We've pretty much gone over everything we need to know, so we should head out... How about you, Tighnari? What are you going to do?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I'll stay here for now. I still want to try a few more things to help Haypasia.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If you're planning to go into the desert, start by heading for Caravan Ribat. That'll be your fastest route.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Come find me here if there's anything else I can do to help. May the spirit of wisdom go with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Tighnari! Hopefully Haypasia will feel better soon! We're off, then.

choices.text: We must stop them no matter what.
The Fatui may have fanned the flames.
Haypasia also showed us a so-called divine consciousness...
I just received some new intel.
"Starlight" refers to the people of the desert.
"Illusions and lies" refer to the Akademiya's plans.
We can't let The Doctor figure out what we're up to.
Our minds swapped places.
What just happened?
*gasp*

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I had already made up my mind to be honest with you, so I didn't try to hide my current condition... Don't worry about me, I'll be fine.
